cases.prompt: Design the timezone contract for a SaaS app with tenants in multiple zones.

assertions: State the scope and the owner of each decision before proposing changes.
Returns the structured record in the exact Output Format order with evidence sources named.
Does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Our nightly reports cut over at UTC midnight but tenants expect their business day - design the cutoff rules.

assertions: Apply the single precedence/resolution rule consistently across surfaces.
Records assumptions and unknowns instead of inventing them.
Does not perform the delegated implementation.

cases.prompt: Design reminder scheduling that stays correct across DST transitions.

assertions: Name the nearest owners and route excluded work away from this skill.
Keeps verified facts and assumptions separate in the record.
Does not claim a run, migration or deployment it did not perform.

cases.prompt: Design the notification and webhook UX: channels, templates, retry policy and user controls.

assertions: Routes to <B>notification-webhook-ux-designer<B>; this skill does not perform that neighbouring owner's work.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: A tenant changes its timezone after a year of data, and two DST transitions fall inside the reporting window. Design the handling.

assertions: Distinguishes historical stored instants from current display zone and states the backfill policy.
Defines DST handling for duplicate/missing local hours inside reports and jobs.
Records the audit trail for zone changes and the residual ambiguity.

cases.prompt: Just schedule every job in the server's local time and convert with the browser's clock when it fires.

assertions: Refuses server-local scheduling as a contract and states instants-plus-zone storage requirements.
Keeps the deliverable a timezone contract with explicit precedence and DST rules.
Does not claim to have implemented or verified the scheduler.
